meta.title: Scale Test - Break It On Purpose

modules.intro: Record what happened, from the score sheet and from your own eyes.
modules.title: The Pull
modules.aiNote: No AI on this module. You were at the rig; nothing else was.

items: My scale article was pulled at the rig
I read my breaking load off the score sheet and wrote it down
I photographed the fracture before putting it away

levels.label: Complete
levels.descriptor: Article pulled, load read from the score sheet, both pieces kept and the fracture photographed.

levels.label: Developing
levels.descriptor: Article was pulled but the load, the pieces or the photograph is missing.

rubric.criterion: The article was tested and the result recorded from the rig

modules.intro: The rig tells you how much. Your own part tells you where. Compare that to what the simulation predicted.
modules.title: Where It Broke
modules.aiNote: Ask it what a fracture surface tells you. Do not ask it to explain your own break; you are the one who saw it.

blocks.content:
Upload your fracture photograph. Get close, get the broken face in focus, and put something in the frame for scale if you can.

You have had a prediction sitting in your notebook since the simulation lab. This is the day you find out whether it was right. A wrong prediction is worth the same marks as a right one here, as long as you say plainly which it was.

blocks.prompt: Where did it break, described on the part? Did it snap, or did it pull open and stop being a hook?
Your simulation put the red somewhere. Is that where it actually broke? Say which, and if it was not, where the break was instead.

blocks.content:
### Before you leave

Start V3 now, while the broken piece is still in your hand. You do not have to finish it, but it has to be **sliceable** by the end of the block, because there are two print windows today and only three left after that.

A hook that waits gets one chance. A hook that is ready now gets five.

### Sources

- Hook Design and Manufacturing Guide, Where Hooks Break and Tournament Rules tabs.
- Your own V2 simulation study and your own scale article.
- Shigley's Mechanical Engineering Design, 10th edition, Budynas and Nisbett, McGraw-Hill, 2015. Stress concentration and modes of failure.
- IDEA AI Use Policy.

levels.label: Complete
levels.descriptor: The broken face is visible and in focus and is this student's own article.

levels.label: Developing
levels.descriptor: A photograph of the article where the fracture cannot be made out.

rubric.criterion: Photograph of the actual fracture on this student's article

levels.label: Complete
levels.descriptor: Names the feature of the hook where it failed and says whether it fractured or deformed open.

levels.label: Proficient
levels.descriptor: Says where it broke without saying how, or the reverse.

levels.label: Developing
levels.descriptor: Says it broke without saying where on the part.

rubric.criterion: Locates the break on the part and names the failure mode

levels.label: Complete
levels.descriptor: States plainly whether the break matched the red spot, and where it went instead if it did not. A miss stated clearly is full marks.

levels.label: Developing
levels.descriptor: Refers to the simulation without saying clearly whether it called the location.

levels.label: Absent
levels.descriptor: Nothing written, or claims a match with no location given.

rubric.criterion: Compares the actual break against the simulation prediction, honestly
